statement: A string is accepted as an ISBN-13 only when its 12 leading digits, weighted alternately 1 and 3 starting with 1, plus the 13th digit sum to a multiple of 10, so "9780306406157" is valid and "9780306406158" is invalid.

faults.description: Weights are applied starting with 3 instead of 1, so valid ISBNs such as 9780306406157 fail the check.
The sum is accepted when it is off by one from a multiple of 10, so a wrong check digit such as 9780306406158 passes.

statement: A stored title is trimmed and every internal run of whitespace is collapsed to a single space, and a title that is empty after trimming is rejected with InvalidTitleError.

faults.description: Internal whitespace runs are replaced with nothing instead of a single space, so "The   Quiet  River" becomes "TheQuietRiver".
The empty-title guard is removed, so a blank or whitespace-only title is accepted instead of raising InvalidTitleError.
faults.find: if (title === '') throw new InvalidTitleError('Title must not be empty');

statement: A "Last, First" author string yields the trimmed last and first names, and a comma-free string yields the whole trimmed string as last name with an empty first name.

faults.description: Last and first names are swapped in the result, so "Okafor, Ada" yields last "Ada" and first "Okafor".
The first name is no longer trimmed, so "Okafor,  Ada " yields first name "  Ada " with surrounding whitespace.
A single-name author gets the placeholder "N/A" as first name instead of the empty string.

statement: An exact ISBN lookup compares the query after R1 normalization, so a hyphenated or spaced ISBN finds the record stored under its 13-digit form, and a query that is not a valid ISBN-13 fails with InvalidIsbnError instead of returning no result.

faults.description: Normalization strips only hyphens and not spaces, so a spaced ISBN such as "978 0 306 40615 7" is no longer normalized and the lookup fails.
The invalid-ISBN guard is removed, so a lookup with an invalid ISBN no longer throws InvalidIsbnError and returns no result instead.

statement: A title prefix query is normalized like a stored title (trimmed, internal whitespace runs collapsed to one space) before it is matched against the start of each normalized title.

faults.description: Trimming is dropped from title normalization, so a query with leading whitespace such as "  the qu" keeps a leading space and no longer matches "The Quiet River".
Only single spaces are matched for replacement, so runs of whitespace are not collapsed and the query "the   qu" no longer matches "The Quiet River".

statement: Search results are ordered by title ascending ignoring case, with records of equal titles ordered by ascending publication year.

faults.description: The title comparison direction is reversed, so results come out in descending title order.
Year tie-breaking is descending instead of ascending, so "Atlas" (2010) precedes "atlas" (1999).

statement: The summary groups records into decades by rounding the year down to a multiple of ten and lists each non-empty decade with its count in ascending order.

faults.description: The decade is rounded to nearest instead of down, so 1999 lands in the 2000s.
The ascending-order sort comparator is replaced by a truncated, syntactically invalid expression, so decade ordering is no longer defined.

statement: A citation reads `Last, F. (Year). Title. ISBN` with the first name's initial uppercased, omits the initial for single-name authors, and for several authors shows only the first followed by ", et al." before the year.

faults.description: The author parser never reads a first name, so the citation loses the initial and shows "Okafor (2004)" instead of "Okafor, A. (2004)".
The ", et al." suffix is added only when there are more than two authors, so a two-author record is cited as a single author.
The initial is no longer uppercased, so a first name "ada" is cited as "a." instead of "A.".
